title: A test loop guarded by a filter must prove the filter keeps at least one item
rule: When a test asserts inside a loop or an `if let` that only runs for some results (`.filter(|m| !m.chars.is_empty())`, `if let Some(x)`), first assert that the data has at least one such result, or pick test data that is known to produce one (a named near-miss row) and assert on that row directly. A loop over zero matching items asserts nothing, so a regression in the printed or computed value passes.
rationale: E26.2 (#165): the check that `fm search --supports` prints the missing characters looped over hits with non-empty `missing`, but every MockApi hit for sr-Cyrl covered fully, so the loop never ran and a broken MISSING column passed.
